column3: The Hebrew calls the building “his house” twice and separately says that he built and completed it; BSB combines this as completing the construction of his palace.

The Hebrew leaves the maker unnamed; BSB supplies Solomon.
The Hebrew says “from floor to floor”; BSB says “from floor to ceiling.”
The Hebrew says “his house” and explicitly names another courtyard; BSB uses “the palace” and “set further back.”
The Hebrew says “all these” without the noun “buildings” and uses singular “the saw”; BSB supplies “buildings” and uses plural “saws.”
The Hebrew says “stones of ten cubits” and “stones of eight cubits”; BSB supplies “some” and specifies length.
The Hebrew says “costly stones” and “cedar”; BSB uses “high-grade stones” and supplies “beams.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew coordinates Solomon’s sending and taking Huram as actions; BSB makes bringing him the purpose of sending.
The Hebrew says that he was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge and leaves him unnamed; BSB names Huram and renders the filling as having great skill.
The Hebrew states the first pillar’s height and the second pillar’s circumference separately; BSB applies both measurements to each pillar.
The Hebrew separately states five cubits for each of the two capitals; BSB combines this as “each capital five cubits high.”
The Hebrew separately states seven for the first capital and seven for the second; BSB combines this as “seven for each capital.”
The Hebrew says the capitals were on top of “the pomegranates”; BSB says “atop the pillars.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with “the second capital”; BSB uses “each capital.”
The Hebrew says “right” and “left” and repeats the erecting of the pillars; BSB uses “south” and “north” and condenses the repeated action.
